text:
Customer_SRE_Maria: heads up — after our peering change to the transit-gw yesterday, our Redwood Private endpoints are intermittently unreachable from our VPC. Internal DNS lookups to the redwood private resolver are failing and API calls to https://private.redwood.example.local time out. Noticed BGP is up but routes aren't showing on our side.

Support_Alex: thanks Maria — can you paste the output of `show ip bgp summary` and `ip route` from your edge? Also any tcpdump on UDP/53 or ESP packets would help.

Customer_SRE_Maria: pasted truncated outputs below. BGP shows neighbor 10.10.10.1 established, 0 prefixes received. `ip route` doesn't have routes to 10.0.0.0/16 (Redwood svc).
```
BGP neighbor is 10.10.10.1, remote AS 65020, state = Established, prefixes = 0
LocalAS 65010, remoteAS 65020
Received prefixes: 0
```

Customer_SRE_Maria: tcpdump on eth0 shows DNS queries going to 10.1.2.2 but no replies; traceroute to ocsp.redwood-ocsp.private shows first hop 10.10.10.254 then * * *.

EngNet_Jamie: oof. BGP established but 0 prefixes is the key. On our side (Redwood peering) can you confirm you didn't apply an export policy or route-filter on the tenant side? Common causes: community-based suppress, route-map with `deny`, or `suppress-protocol bgp` on TGW. Also check if you accidentally applied `no-advertise` or `no-export` communities.

Customer_SRE_Maria: we didn't touch communities intentionally. Our infra team did switch on a transit-gw inbound route filter during the peering change.

EngInfra_Ravi: @Customer_SRE_Maria can you run `show bgp ipv4 unicast neighbors 10.10.10.1 received-routes` and `show route-map`? If the TGW has a route filter, it might be stripping propagated prefixes so Redwood never sees your VPC subnets, and vice versa.

Customer_SRE_Maria: output: `received-routes: 0` and our route-map has a deny for `10.0.0.0/8` for another tenant — looks like a broad deny was applied. I think that accidentally matched more than intended.

Support_Alex: that explains why DNS/OCSP fail: the resolver IPs are reachable only via the Redwood route advertised into the VPC. With no routes, packets never hit the correct next-hop and time out. Two symptoms: (1) BGP suppression of prefixes, (2) no return path for UDP/53 and TCP to OCSP.

Security_Kate: also confirm your egress allowlist/firewall rules — some customers block outbound to external OCSP responders or DNS and rely on the private resolvers. If routes are missing, traffic may egress to internet path and be blocked by your deny-list.

Customer_SRE_Maria: checked iptables — no explicit outbound deny. But our proxy/egress appliance has a restrictive allowlist. Traceroute shows traffic hitting transit and getting blackholed.

EngNet_Jamie: suggested immediate mitigations: 1) remove the overly-broad deny in the TGW route-map for the affected prefixes, 2) add a temporary static route for the Redwood resolver IPs via the transit-gw so DNS/OCSP can return, 3) validate BGP after change (`show ip bgp` should show prefixes >0).

Customer_SRE_Maria: applied a scoped fix: narrowed the deny to the specific tenant prefix and added static routes for 10.1.2.0/24 -> next-hop 10.10.10.254. Testing now...

DeployBot: canary-check: private-api-prod: health check failures -> 3 failing out of 10 -> alert triggered.

Customer_SRE_Maria: DNS lookups now returning answers for internal resolver. `dig @10.1.2.2 internal.redwood.svc +short` returns IP. API calls are responding (latency normal).

EngInfra_Ravi: confirm `show ip bgp summary` now shows prefixes received?

Customer_SRE_Maria: yes — `prefixes = 42` and routes visible.

Support_Alex: great. Root cause: overly-broad route-map/filter applied during peering change suppressed Redwood prefixes and broke return path for DNS/OCSP, manifesting as API timeouts. Secondary issue: egress allowlist on customer appliance amplified outage by blocking fallback to internet-based resolvers/OCSP.

Security_Kate: next steps for remediation and prevention: - Create a pre-change checklist for route-map changes (verify prefix-lists and minimize `deny` ranges). - Add a test BGP neighbor and dry-run to confirm prefix visibility. - Document required egress allowlist entries for OCSP/responder and private resolver ranges.

EngNet_Jamie: Redwood-side action: add monitoring to detect neighbors with 0 prefixes or sudden <10% prefix drop and alert SRE on-call. Also add operational docs showing `show bgp ... received-routes` as first check.

Customer_SRE_Maria: will schedule a follow-up call with our network team to review TGW config and rollback plan. Thanks everyone for the quick help. :pray:

Support_Alex: marking incident as resolved for now — will keep open for postmortem notes.

Customer_SRE_Maria: logging for postmortem: change window 2026-03-17 02:00 UTC, misconfigured route-map applied at 02:12, fixed at 03:05. Impacted: private API calls and internal DNS for ~53 minutes.

EngInfra_Ravi: noted. I'll draft a short RCA and link configs.

DeployBot: incident-status: resolved -> monitoring.
